aboutStory:
Built the same way as the Singapore and Las Vegas guides — researched remotely using public GPS data, race reports, and Wikipedia, not walked in person.

Albert Park is a public park that stays open to walkers, joggers, and cyclists all year — it only closes for the race weekend. The 2022 layout change (removing the Turn 9/10 chicane) shifted every corner number after it down by two, which took real care to get right using an independent source confirming the old-to-new mapping.

Treat it as a work in progress rather than ground truth, and if you walk it yourself, corrections and reports are very welcome.
helpSubtitle: Fan-made walking guide — S/F line + all 14 corners of the Albert Park Circuit
helpOfflineNote: After first load, the app and map tiles work fully offline. This makes it useful as a general Albert Park GPS map even when roaming doesn't work.
quirkTitle: A circuit that shares its roads with black swans
quirkBody: Albert Park Lake is home to a breeding population of black swans, which frequently wander onto the road — sometimes with up to five cygnets in tow — causing traffic delays for everyday drivers around the park, race weekend or not.
welcomeSub: Walk all 14 corners of the Albert Park Circuit, looping Albert Park Lake just south of Melbourne's CBD.
welcomeSteps: Start at the S/F marker on Lakeside Drive — that's where the race starts and ends each lap.
Enable GPS and the app follows you — auto-advancing to the next corner as you approach. Orange markers mean you're close. Use Auto to toggle this.
Works offline — once loaded, the map and app work without internet. Useful as a general Albert Park GPS map if roaming doesn't work.
Tap Help anytime for full details on all features.
